page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the arm64 architecture, powered by 32 dedicated physical cores of Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance features a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory configuration with 128.0 GB of system RAM supported by 128 MB of L3 cache. Storage needs are served by 1888 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD capacity, while graphic acceleration is omitted with zero discrete GPUs present.

Performance benchmarks show notable strength in multi-threaded computation and memory subsystem operations. The instance achieves top-tier results in uncached memory read bandwidth reaching 448.6 GB/sec, write bandwidth of 188.32 GB/sec, and synthetic database operation scores. Multi-core execution ranks in the upper quartile across stress-ng tests and software compilation with Clang. In contrast, single-core processing scores in Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier, and large-scale language model inference exhibits lower processing rates due to the absence of specialized matrix instruction sets.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the ARM Neoverse-N2 implementation provides high compute density and low power overhead relative to its thread capacity. The combination of dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores and fast local NVMe storage provides strong resource predictability for data-heavy workloads. The D32pds_v6 is suitable for relational and NoSQL databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, high-concurrency static web serving, and distributed data transformation tasks.

Performance evaluation reveals exceptional memory subsystem bandwidth, with uncached large-block reads exceeding 448 GB/sec, placing memory throughput and database operation metrics in the top tier. With its combination of fast local storage and high concurrent throughput, the D32pds_v6 is engineered for database workloads, continuous integration build farms, static web hosting, and distributed data transformation pipelines.
